title: Commission a small-office DHCP service
prompt: Complete the router DHCP configuration for a new small office. Use the addressing plan to choose the dynamic range and options that clients should receive. Do not lease the manually assigned infrastructure addresses.
briefing: The LAN is 10.24.8.0/24. The router LAN interface is 10.24.8.1. The approved internal DNS resolver is 10.24.8.5.
Manually addressed infrastructure occupies .1 through .49. Policy allocates .50 through .149 to the dynamic pool; .150 through .254 is reserved for future static assignments.
Enter the full start and end addresses, subnet mask, default gateway and DNS resolver delivered by DHCP. No subnet design or address is left to guess.
explanation: Lease 10.24.8.50 through 10.24.8.149, using mask 255.255.255.0, gateway 10.24.8.1 and DNS 10.24.8.5. The pool must avoid manually assigned infrastructure and the reserved future range. The gateway routes traffic; the separate DNS service resolves names.
reference:
Current draft: pool 10.24.8.2–10.24.8.254
Mask: 255.255.0.0
Router option: 10.24.8.5
DNS option: 10.24.8.1

title: Restore the archive server mirror pair
prompt: The archive server RAID 10 array reports a degraded mirror pair after one member failed. Inspect the controller evidence, identify the failed member, select the compatible spare and rebuild. Do not remove its healthy mirror partner.
briefing: This is a fictional training console; type help for syntax. A current verified backup exists and hot replacement is approved for this enclosure.
The four-member RAID 10 array consists of mirror pairs bays 1/2 and 3/4. Each member is a 4 TB SATA disk. The failed disk must be identified by serial, not guessed from a bay label.
Two spares are on the shelf: SN-R800 (2 TB SATA) and SN-R900 (4 TB SATA). Replacement capacity must be at least 4 TB; the controller confirms SN-R900 is compatible.

Use raid status, raid drives, raid identify <failed-serial>, raid replace <failed-serial> <spare-serial>, and raid rebuild. Inspect status before identifying, identify before replacement, and replace before rebuilding.
explanation: The controller identifies failed SN-R402 in bay 4. After raid status and raid drives, run raid identify SN-R402, raid replace SN-R402 SN-R900, and raid rebuild. SN-R800 is undersized. Keep the healthy bay-3 mirror partner online; losing both members of that pair would lose the array. Rebuild completion restores the mirror protection, but RAID is not a backup.
reference: Maintenance ticket: archive server remains online but has lost redundancy in one mirror pair. Inspect the console inventory before selecting a disk.

raid_config.degraded_detail: Mirror pair bays 3/4 has only one healthy member.

title: Restore a survey phone profile
prompt: A surveyor can browse over Wi-Fi but has five independent mobile configuration problems. Select the smallest appropriate correction for each symptom from the verified settings.
briefing: The Bluetooth rangefinder is powered on but not discoverable. Its manual requires pairing mode before the phone can find it.
The survey app needs location only during active surveys. Device location services are on, but the app permission is denied.
Company mail works. The same account Calendar switch is off, although events are visible in the company web calendar.
The carrier confirms an active cellular data plan and coverage. Wi-Fi is unavailable in the field, and the phone Cellular Data switch is off.
Photo uploads exhaust the monthly plan. The approved backup app supports automatic Wi-Fi-only uploads, and company Wi-Fi is available after each shift.

options.label: Put rangefinder in pairing mode, then select it on the phone
Allow location while using the app
Reset the working mail account password
Enable Calendar sync for the existing company account
Enable cellular data for the active plan
Allow all automatic uploads over cellular
Schedule automatic uploads for Wi-Fi only

explanation: Enable rangefinder pairing mode; allow location while using the survey app; enable Calendar for the working company account; turn on cellular data for the active plan; and keep automatic photo uploads on Wi-Fi. Each action addresses a separate verified configuration rather than replacing functioning hardware.
reference: Diagnostic record: radios and subscription hardware pass checks. No account password error is reported. All settings can be changed within company policy.

title: Place three training workloads
prompt: Create three VMs using the approved workload profiles. Translate the profile table and storage requirements into the allocations below. Host capacity available to guests is 16 vCPU and 64 GiB RAM; overcommit is prohibited.
briefing: Profiles: Small = 2 vCPU / 4 GiB; Medium = 4 vCPU / 12 GiB; Large = 6 vCPU / 24 GiB. Use the exact approved profile, not the largest that fits.
Database training VM: Medium profile and low-latency storage. Remote desktop lab: Large profile and low-latency storage. Internal web sandbox: Small profile and general-purpose storage.

Storage catalog: /datastores/nvme is the low-latency datastore; /datastores/capacity is the general-purpose datastore; /datastores/backup is reserved for backup files, not running VM disks. All have enough free space.
Exceeding either host CPU or RAM capacity invalidates all CPU/RAM criteria; storage placement is scored independently. Paths are training labels, not paths on your computer.
explanation: The Medium database gets 4 vCPU/12 GiB on /datastores/nvme; the Large remote desktop gets 6 vCPU/24 GiB on /datastores/nvme; the Small web sandbox gets 2 vCPU/4 GiB on /datastores/capacity. Total allocation is 12 vCPU and 40 GiB, within the 16/64 budget. Backup storage is not an approved runtime location.
reference: The hypervisor and CPU virtualization features are already working. Allocate only guest resources; host overhead has already been deducted.

title: Interpret a cooling interlock
prompt: A newly serviced workstation halts during startup. Read its supplied vendor diagnostic legend and choose the affected subsystem and corrective service action. Do not bypass the interlock.
briefing: The service log records display code F2 and the message CPU_FAN: 0 RPM. Visual inspection confirms the CPU fan is motionless while the case fans spin.
The CPU fan plug is fully seated on the correct header, its blades are unobstructed, and a technician has verified that the header supply works.
This model-specific legend is supplied for the task: F1 = memory initialization failure; F2 = CPU cooling fan not operating; F3 = boot device absent. Codes are not universal across manufacturers.
An approved replacement CPU fan assembly is available. Select the diagnosis and safest corrective action based on the evidence.

options.label: Power down, replace the failed fan assembly as documented, then verify fan operation and temperatures
Disable the fan interlock and continue booting
Reseat the DIMMs as the primary repair

explanation: F2, zero fan RPM and a stationary fan on a verified working supply identify the CPU cooling fan. Power down and replace the failed assembly using the approved service procedure, then verify rotation, reported speed and operating temperature. Bypassing the interlock leaves the CPU without its required cooling.
reference:
Workstation model: Harbor S2 (fictional)
POST: F2
CPU_FAN: 0 RPM
Case fans: normal
Header supply and connector seating: verified

title: Service the keyboard ribbon
prompt: Several keys on a laptop stopped working after a keyboard replacement. An external keyboard works. With power and the internal battery disconnected, the technician finds the keyboard ribbon resting loosely in a zero-insertion-force connector. What should the technician do?

options.text: Replace the external USB keyboard
Apply adhesive over the ribbon without opening the latch
Force the ribbon farther in while the latch remains closed
Seat the ribbon evenly and secure the connector latch according to the service manual

explanation: A ZIF connector depends on correct ribbon insertion and its locking latch. Follow the service procedure with power isolated; force or glue can damage the connector. A working external keyboard does not repair the internal ribbon connection.

title: Protect privacy at a shared desk
prompt: A sales representative handles confidential records on a laptop in a public reception area. Which accessory most directly reduces viewing of the screen by people sitting to either side?

options.text: A matte anti-glare coating without a privacy specification
A fitted display privacy filter
A chassis cable lock
A webcam privacy shutter

explanation: A privacy filter restricts viewing from the sides. A camera shutter blocks the webcam, a chassis lock deters removal, and an anti-glare coating reduces reflections without necessarily limiting viewing angles.

title: Reconnect the wireless antennas
prompt: During an approved laptop WLAN-card replacement, two miniature antenna leads are disconnected. Which TWO actions support a correct reassembly?

options.text: Trim the leads to remove excess cable around the display hinge
Connect both antenna leads to the same terminal for stronger reception
Route the antenna leads through the specified channels, clear of hinges and screws
Leave the auxiliary lead disconnected because it only supplies power
Reconnect each lead to the terminal identified in the service documentation

explanation: The terminal assignment and cable routing must follow the model-specific service instructions. Pinched, shortened or misconnected antenna leads can degrade radio performance; the auxiliary connection is not a power supply.

title: Capture pressure-sensitive sketches
prompt: A designer wants to vary digital brush thickness by changing pen pressure on a mobile drawing surface. Which accessory should be selected?

options.text: A presentation pointer that sends only next/previous commands
A passive capacitive stylus without pressure support
A basic touchpad without pen-pressure input
A pressure-sensitive active stylus supported by the device

explanation: A supported pressure-sensitive active stylus reports pressure to compatible drawing software. A passive pointer or ordinary touchpad does not provide the requested pen-pressure input; a presentation pointer sends control commands rather than expressive drawing data.

title: Expand a desk with a port replicator
prompt: A laptop already runs its applications at the required speed. A user needs one supported connection at the desk for an external keyboard, wired network and USB storage. Which purchase most directly meets this need?

options.text: A USB-C power adapter with no data ports
A compatible port replicator with Ethernet and USB ports
A USB hub with no network adapter or Ethernet port
A wireless display adapter with no peripheral ports

explanation: The compatible port replicator supplies both USB peripheral ports and Ethernet in the stated desk connection. A USB-only hub lacks the requested network connection, a display adapter does not replicate the peripheral ports, and a power-only adapter supplies no data connectivity.

title: Restore the missing calendar
prompt: A new phone receives company email successfully. Calendar events remain absent, although the same account shows them in the web calendar. The account settings show Mail enabled and Calendar disabled. What is the best next action?

options.text: Enable calendar synchronization for that account
Replace the account outgoing mail server setting
Remove and recreate the working Wi-Fi profile
Clear all Bluetooth pairings on the phone

explanation: Calendar is a separate synchronization category from Mail. Enable it for the working account. Working mail and web access provide no evidence that the Wi-Fi profile or outgoing mail configuration needs replacement; Bluetooth does not carry the account calendar synchronization.

title: Stop roaming data use
prompt: An employee traveling abroad must avoid cellular roaming data charges while retaining access to hotel Wi-Fi. Which setting change directly meets the requirement?

options.text: Enable the phone hotspot and leave roaming enabled
Reduce screen brightness and leave roaming data enabled
Disable data roaming and continue using Wi-Fi
Disable Wi-Fi but leave cellular data roaming enabled

explanation: Disable data roaming to prevent roaming cellular data while leaving Wi-Fi available. A hotspot can consume cellular data, turning off Wi-Fi can increase reliance on cellular, and display brightness does not control roaming. This setting alone does not address possible voice or SMS charges.

title: Move photographs through a cable
prompt: A camera phone charges when connected to a laptop, but the supplied cable is documented as charge-only. The user needs local wired photo transfer. What is the best replacement?

options.text: A charge-only cable with a higher current rating
A passive USB power meter with no data pass-through
A compatible USB cable that supports data transfer
A USB power adapter with the same connector

explanation: The complete USB path must support data, not just power. A compatible data cable meets the stated need; higher current capacity, a power adapter or a device without data pass-through does not add data conductors. The phone may also require unlocking and transfer authorization.

title: Pair a headset with a replacement phone
prompt: A headset is still automatically connecting to a retired phone beside the user. The replacement phone cannot discover it. Which TWO actions should the technician take before testing audio on the replacement?

options.text: Assign a static IP address to the headset
Place the headset in discoverable pairing mode and select it on the replacement phone
Change the phone cellular access-point settings
Change the Wi-Fi security mode on the replacement phone
Disconnect the headset from the retired phone

explanation: Disconnect the existing headset connection and use discoverable pairing mode to establish the new Bluetooth relationship. Wi-Fi security, IP configuration and cellular access-point settings do not make this local Bluetooth headset discoverable.

title: Choose the correct mobile battery
prompt: A serviceable laptop battery has lost runtime after years of use. Three packs fit inside the case, but only one is listed for this laptop model and required voltage. Which should be installed?

options.text: Any pack that physically fits, regardless of voltage
A pack with damaged insulation if its capacity is higher
The manufacturer-approved compatible pack with the required electrical specification
The highest-voltage pack to increase performance

explanation: Physical fit and advertised capacity are insufficient. Match the approved part, electrical ratings and service instructions. Incorrect voltage or damaged insulation creates a hazard and is not an acceptable runtime upgrade.

title: Allow location for delivery check-ins
prompt: A delivery app opens normally and uploads photographs, but cannot attach the current position. System location services are on, and the app permission is set to Deny. What change directly addresses the fault?

options.text: Reset the app mail synchronization schedule
Change the Wi-Fi DNS server
Grant the app appropriate location permission while it is in use
Re-pair the Bluetooth headset

explanation: Grant the survey app appropriate location access while in use. An enabled system location service does not override an app-specific denial. Mail synchronization, headset pairing and DNS settings do not change that permission.

title: Permit a Windows file share
prompt: A workstation reaches a file server by IP, but a firewall blocks direct SMB file sharing. Which destination TCP port should be allowed for modern direct-hosted SMB?
explanation: Direct-hosted SMB uses TCP 445. LDAP uses 389, POP3 uses 110, and RDP normally uses 3389. Allow only the required service between authorized endpoints.

title: Distinguish two mailbox protocols
prompt: A user reads mail on a phone and a desktop and needs folders and read state synchronized on the server. Which protocol is designed for this mailbox access model?

options.text: IMAP
POP3 configured to download and remove messages from the server
SMTP
NTP

explanation: IMAP maintains server-held mailbox folders and state for access from several clients. POP3 configured to download and remove mail conflicts with that requirement. SMTP transfers outgoing mail and NTP synchronizes clocks; neither provides the requested mailbox model.

title: Trace DHCP traffic
prompt: A packet capture follows a client obtaining an IPv4 lease using DHCP. Which TWO UDP ports identify the DHCP server and client services?
explanation: DHCP for IPv4 uses UDP server port 67 and client port 68. DNS uses 53, IMAP normally uses TCP 143, and direct SMB uses TCP 445. The client can request configuration before it has a usable leased address.

title: Reduce channel overlap in a dense office
prompt: A survey shows neighboring 5 GHz access points consuming overlapping wide channels. Peak single-client throughput is less important than consistent service for many nearby cells. Which change is most appropriate to evaluate?

options.text: Increase channel width on all access points
Increase every access point transmit power to maximum without revising channels
Use narrower channels with a coordinated channel plan
Set every access point to the same widest channel

explanation: Narrower channels can allow a more effective non-overlapping channel plan in a dense deployment, at the cost of peak throughput per channel. Wider overlapping channels or blanket maximum transmit power can increase contention instead of improving predictable shared service.

title: Synchronize log timestamps
prompt: Investigators cannot compare events across several servers because their clocks disagree by minutes. Which network service most directly keeps system time aligned?

options.text: DHCP
Syslog collection alone
DNS forwarding
NTP

explanation: NTP synchronizes clocks to time sources. Syslog centralizes messages but does not itself synchronize the source clocks; DNS resolves names and DHCP provides network configuration. Configuring a time source through another service still relies on a time-synchronization mechanism.

title: Publish a mail destination
prompt: A company moves its inbound email service to a new provider. Which DNS record type directs other mail servers to the mail exchanger for the company domain?

options.text: MX
TXT
CNAME
A

explanation: MX records direct mail delivery to a domain mail exchanger. A records map hostnames to IPv4, CNAME records make aliases and TXT records hold text policies or other data. An MX target must also resolve to an address, but an address record alone does not select the domain mail exchanger.

title: Terminate an incoming fiber service
prompt: An ISP delivers fiber to a small office. Which device commonly terminates the provider optical service and presents an Ethernet handoff for the office router?

options.text: A cable modem
A passive optical patch panel with no service-termination electronics
An optical network terminal
A DSL modem

explanation: An ONT terminates the provider optical access service and commonly presents Ethernet. Cable and DSL modems terminate other access media. A passive optical patch panel only connects fibers; it does not perform active service termination.

title: Recognize an automatic link-local address
prompt: A technician documenting a SOHO network sees address 169.254.22.14/16 on one client. Which description correctly classifies the address?

options.text: The IPv4 loopback address for that host
An IPv4 link-local address, not a normally routed internet address
A multicast group address
A public IPv4 address suitable for publishing the office website

explanation: 169.254.0.0/16 is IPv4 link-local space, commonly self-assigned when DHCP is unavailable. It supports local-link communication under appropriate conditions and is not normally routed. Loopback and multicast use different ranges.

title: Separate fixed addresses from leases
prompt: A small office manually assigns static addresses .10 through .19 to infrastructure on its /24 LAN. The DHCP scope currently includes .2 through .200. Which TWO statements describe an appropriate change?

options.text: Lengthen all leases without changing address allocations
Exclude .10 through .19 from dynamic leasing
Keep manually assigned addresses documented to prevent overlapping assignments
Add DNS A records while leaving the overlapping DHCP scope unchanged
Shorten all leases without changing address allocations

explanation: Exclude the manually allocated range from dynamic leasing and document the assignments. DNS records do not prevent DHCP from offering an overlapping address. Shorter or longer lease durations change timing, not which addresses the server is allowed to lease.

title: Select a neighborhood network scope
prompt: A provider links municipal offices across one city using a metropolitan fiber service. Which network scope best describes the city-wide interconnection?

options.text: PAN
WAN spanning several continents
LAN limited to one building
MAN

explanation: A MAN connects sites across a metropolitan area. A PAN serves a personal area, a single-building LAN is smaller in scope, and a WAN spanning continents describes a broader geographic interconnection.

title: Find an unlabeled cable
prompt: An unused copper cable runs from a wall jack to one of many disconnected cables in a wiring closet. Which tool pair is most appropriate for tracing that cable without configuring an IP network?

options.text: Wi-Fi analyzer and signal-strength survey
Tone generator and probe
Copper loopback plug and a host NIC diagnostic
Crimper and spare modular plugs

explanation: A tone generator and probe trace a suitable disconnected copper cable without an IP configuration. A crimper installs connectors, a loopback helps test an interface, and a Wi-Fi analyzer examines radio networks rather than identifying this disconnected copper run.

title: Consolidate perimeter inspection
prompt: A branch wants one appliance to provide firewall filtering, intrusion inspection and web-content filtering. Which appliance category best fits?

options.text: A basic unmanaged Ethernet switch
A DNS caching resolver
A print server
Unified threat management

explanation: UTM combines multiple security functions, such as firewalling, intrusion inspection and content filtering, in one appliance category. Basic unmanaged switching, print service and DNS caching do not provide the requested collection of perimeter controls.

title: Keep an alias after a server change
prompt: Users access reports.example.test, which should follow the canonical host analytics.example.test rather than have an independently maintained address record. Which DNS record type fits?

options.text: MX
TXT
AAAA
CNAME

explanation: A CNAME creates an alias to the canonical hostname so resolution follows that name. AAAA supplies a direct IPv6 mapping instead; MX directs mail delivery and TXT holds text data. Those records do not provide the requested general hostname alias.

title: Add PoE without replacing a switch
prompt: An existing non-PoE switch has spare data ports. One new access point supports an identified IEEE PoE standard and has no nearby mains outlet. Which TWO checks or purchases meet the requirement?

options.text: Use a passive patch panel as the power source
Select the injector solely by its RJ45 connector shape
Verify that the injector supplies the access point's required power under the supported PoE standard
Use a PoE injector compatible with the access point and Ethernet link
Use an Ethernet surge protector with no power injection

explanation: Use an injector compatible with the link, the access point PoE standard and its power requirement. Connector shape alone cannot establish compatibility. A passive patch panel or surge protector with no power injection cannot supply the access point power.

title: Identify an interactive remote desktop
prompt: A support station is allowed to connect to a Windows remote desktop service on its default port. Which destination TCP port belongs to this service?
explanation: RDP normally uses TCP 3389 and can also use UDP 3389 for supported transports. Telnet uses 23, SMTP relay uses 25, and IMAP uses 143. Actual deployments may restrict or change the service configuration.

title: Match a cable internet handoff
prompt: A home office already has a provider-approved modem connected to coaxial cable. Which broadband access technology is being used?

options.text: Fiber to the premises using an ONT
Cable internet
DSL
Satellite broadband

explanation: Cable broadband uses a provider cable modem on the coaxial network. DSL uses telephone copper, fiber-to-the-premises service uses optical termination, and satellite uses a satellite terminal.

title: Terminate a structured cabling run
prompt: A technician must attach the individual conductors of a horizontal twisted-pair cable to an insulation-displacement patch-panel termination. Which tool is appropriate?

options.text: Punchdown tool
Tone probe
Modular-plug crimping tool
Copper loopback plug

explanation: A punchdown tool seats conductors into insulation-displacement terminals, usually trimming the excess as specified. A crimper fits modular plugs, a tone probe traces cables and a loopback helps test an interface; none substitutes for correct IDC termination.

title: Read an IPv6 local-link address
prompt: A router interface has IPv6 address fe80::1 on its LAN. Which statement best describes its scope?

options.text: The universal IPv6 loopback address
An IPv4-mapped public address
Link-local; it is used on the local link rather than routed across the internet
A globally routable address that must be reachable from all ISPs

explanation: fe80::/10 identifies IPv6 link-local space. Such addresses are useful for local-link functions and may need an interface or zone identifier where ambiguous. IPv6 loopback is ::1, not fe80::1.

title: Centralize network access decisions
prompt: A growing office wants an AAA service for its network devices. Which TWO capabilities belong to AAA?

options.text: Translate private IPv4 addresses to public addresses
Record connection or usage activity for accounting
Lease addresses to client devices
Determine what an authenticated user is permitted to access
Resolve hostnames into IP addresses

explanation: AAA includes authentication, authorization and accounting. Authorization determines permitted access and accounting records usage. NAT, DHCP and DNS respectively translate addresses, lease configuration and resolve names; they are not the requested AAA functions.

title: Track warehouse stock with radio tags
prompt: A warehouse needs to read tagged cartons using radio identification without requiring each carton to join the IP Wi-Fi network. Which technology is most appropriate?

options.text: NFC requiring near-contact presentation at each reader
Infrared line-of-sight remote control
Bluetooth audio streaming
RFID

explanation: RFID tags and readers support radio identification of inventory without each tag becoming a Wi-Fi IP client. The alternatives describe near-contact interaction, audio streaming or line-of-sight control rather than the requested warehouse carton identification.

title: Match smooth motion requirements
prompt: A workstation and cable already support the required native resolution. A user needs smoother motion than the current 60 Hz monitor provides. Which display specification most directly measures how frequently the panel can update its image?

options.text: Contrast ratio
Physical diagonal size
Pixel density alone
Refresh rate

explanation: Refresh rate, measured in hertz, describes display updates per second. A higher supported rate can improve motion presentation when the source provides frames. Contrast, size and pixel density describe other attributes.

title: Avoid a transfer-rate bottleneck
prompt: A technician needs to copy footage from an external SSD at approximately 300 MB/s. The SSD and host support that rate. Which connection has a signaling-rate ceiling sufficient for the target before protocol overhead?

options.text: A USB 2.0 data connection rated at 480 Mb/s
A charge-only USB-C cable with no data support
A compatible USB 3.x data connection rated at 5 Gb/s
A USB 1.1 full-speed connection rated at 12 Mb/s

explanation: 300 MB/s is approximately 2400 Mb/s before overhead. A compatible 5 Gb/s USB data path has a sufficient ceiling; 480 Mb/s USB 2.0 and 12 Mb/s USB 1.1 do not. A charge-only connector provides no data path, and real throughput still depends on the entire storage stack.

title: Decode a DDR module rating
prompt: A memory specification lists a transfer rate of 3200 MT/s. What does MT/s express?

options.text: The number of simultaneously active memory channels
Millions of data transfers per second
Millions of complete clock cycles per second, always identical to the DDR transfer count
The installed memory capacity in millions of bytes

explanation: MT/s means millions of data transfers per second. DDR transfers data on both clock edges, so transfer rate should not be treated as identical to the underlying clock-cycle rate. Capacity and channel count are separate specifications.

title: Enable virtual machines in firmware
prompt: A supported CPU is installed, but a hypervisor reports that hardware virtualization is disabled. Which TWO actions are appropriate?

options.text: Disable all CPU cores except one before retrying the hypervisor
Change the storage controller from AHCI to RAID to expose virtualization
Enable Secure Boot as a substitute for CPU virtualization support
Check UEFI settings for the processor virtualization feature
Enable the supported virtualization feature according to the platform documentation

explanation: Check and enable the supported processor virtualization setting in UEFI. Secure Boot verifies the boot chain, and AHCI/RAID selects a storage-controller mode; neither substitutes for CPU virtualization support. Arbitrarily disabling CPU cores does not enable the feature.

title: Protect data on a striped set
prompt: A user proposes a two-disk RAID 0 array for scratch files that can be regenerated. Which consequence must the user understand?

options.text: Failure of either member can make the striped data unavailable
The array preserves all data after either disk fails
Parity on a third disk protects the two members
Each disk holds a complete copy of all files

explanation: RAID 0 stripes data for capacity and performance but provides no redundancy. A member failure can destroy the usable array. Mirroring and parity protection belong to other layouts; expendable scratch data is different from irreplaceable data.

title: Avoid mixing modular PSU cables
prompt: A technician replaces a modular desktop PSU with a different model. The old detachable cable plugs fit into the new PSU chassis. What should the technician do?

options.text: Reuse the cables if the PSU-side connectors physically fit
Use only cables specified as compatible with the new PSU
Reuse the cables if both PSUs have the same advertised wattage
Reuse the cables if both PSUs carry the same efficiency rating

explanation: Use only cables documented as compatible with the replacement PSU. PSU-side modular pinouts can differ even when connectors fit. Matching advertised wattage or efficiency certification does not prove that the cable pinout is compatible.

title: Set the default print output
prompt: A department wants ordinary documents printed on both sides by default. The printer has a working duplex unit, but the queue defaults to one-sided printing. Which setting should be changed?

options.text: Reverse the page order while leaving simplex selected
Enable two-sided printing in the queue printing defaults
Enable collating while leaving simplex selected
Set two pages per sheet instead of duplex

explanation: Two-sided printing selects duplex output. Multiple pages per sheet changes layout, collation organizes copies, and reverse order changes sequencing. Those settings do not themselves print on the reverse side of the paper.

title: Maintain a receipt printer
prompt: A direct thermal receipt printer produces a light vertical band after prolonged use. The manufacturer recommends cleaning the thermal head. Which maintenance approach is appropriate?

options.text: Power down, allow cooling, and clean with the manufacturer-approved materials
Apply lubricating oil to the heating elements
Run an inkjet nozzle-cleaning cycle on the direct thermal mechanism
Scrape residue off the thermal head with a metal blade

explanation: Follow the documented thermal-head cleaning procedure after shutdown and cooling. A metal blade or oil can damage or contaminate the heating elements. An inkjet nozzle-cleaning cycle does not apply to a direct thermal print mechanism.

title: Connect a digital display and audio
prompt: A conference monitor and laptop both have full-size HDMI ports. One cable must carry digital video and audio between them. Which cable is the direct match?

options.text: A passive USB-A charging cable
HDMI
VGA
RJ11

explanation: HDMI carries digital video and audio between compatible devices. VGA carries analog video without embedded audio. Telephone and charge-only USB connections are not direct replacements for the stated ports.

title: Select a PCIe storage drive
prompt: A motherboard manual lists an M.2 socket wired only for PCIe NVMe storage. Which TWO purchase checks are necessary?

options.text: Ignore the motherboard supported module dimensions
Choose an NVMe drive using the supported PCIe interface
Match the supported module length and keying listed for the socket
Assume an M.2 SATA drive will work because it is also called M.2
Choose a 2.5-inch SATA drive and plug it directly into the M.2 socket

explanation: M.2 describes a physical format, while SATA and PCIe NVMe describe different interfaces. This socket requires a supported NVMe module with the correct physical fit. An M.2 SATA drive is not guaranteed to work in an NVMe-only socket.

title: Match memory to a compact system
prompt: A service manual for a compact desktop specifies DDR5 SO-DIMM memory. Which characteristic distinguishes the requested form factor from a full-size desktop DIMM?

options.text: A shorter DDR5 memory module in the specified SO-DIMM form factor
An external USB-attached memory module
A full-size DIMM with the same DDR generation
A different memory generation using the same capacity rating

explanation: SO-DIMM is a shorter form factor than a full-size DIMM, and the module must also match the specified DDR5 generation and supported capacity. Equal capacity does not make another generation compatible, and USB-attached memory is not the specified system-RAM module.

title: Identify the CPU power connector
prompt: During a motherboard replacement, the main 24-pin power connector is attached, but the documented 8-pin CPU power socket is empty. Which PSU lead should connect there?

options.text: The 24-pin main motherboard lead adapted by forcing its connector
A PCIe graphics power lead selected only for similar appearance
A SATA peripheral power lead without an approved conversion
The compatible EPS/CPU power lead

explanation: Use the compatible EPS/CPU lead for the documented processor power socket. A similar-looking GPU lead, a forced main connector or an unsupported SATA conversion is not a valid substitute. Correct pinout, connector and power rating matter.

title: Choose an LCD panel for shared viewing
prompt: A customer compares a typical IPS LCD with a basic TN LCD for reviewing images with colleagues viewing from the sides. Which IPS characteristic is the most relevant advantage?

options.text: Generally wider viewing angles with more consistent image appearance
No need for a backlight because all IPS pixels emit their own light
A guaranteed higher refresh rate than every TN model
Guaranteed zero motion blur at every frame rate

explanation: Typical IPS panels provide more consistent off-axis viewing than basic TN panels, supporting shared image review. This does not guarantee the highest refresh rate or zero motion blur. IPS is LCD technology and still requires illumination rather than self-emissive pixels.

title: Understand the laser imaging sequence
prompt: In a laser printer, toner must move from the photoconductive drum onto the sheet before the fuser bonds it. Which stage is being described?

options.text: Cleaning the drum after transfer
Processing the page description
Exposing the drum to the laser
Transferring

explanation: The transfer stage moves toner from the drum to the paper. Processing prepares page data, exposure creates the latent image, and cleaning removes residual toner. Fusing then bonds toner to the sheet using heat and pressure.

title: Size a power supply for added drives
prompt: A tower currently runs near its documented PSU output limit. A planned expansion adds several hard drives. What should be included in the power assessment?

options.text: Only the PSU efficiency certification
Total component demand, drive startup demand, suitable connectors and reasonable headroom
Only the sum of disk formatted capacities
Only the fact that spare power connectors exist

explanation: Assess total component demand, drive startup demand, appropriate connectors and suitable headroom. Efficiency certification measures conversion efficiency, disk capacity measures storage, and unused connectors alone do not establish available electrical output.

title: Deploy a shared printer queue
prompt: An office is creating a print-server queue for workstations with supported operating systems. Which TWO configuration tasks directly support reliable client printing?

options.text: Use an unrelated printer driver solely because it installs without an error
Apply the intended queue sharing and access permissions
Install a driver compatible with the printer and client environment
Disable the print spooler on the print server
Point the queue at an unused address instead of the printer

explanation: Deploy a compatible driver and the intended sharing/access permissions. The queue must target the actual printer and the print spooler must run. An unrelated driver can install successfully yet generate unusable output or lack required features.

title: Identify a magnetic drive characteristic
prompt: A workstation stores large archives on a 3.5-inch hard disk. Which specification describes the rotational speed of its magnetic platters?

options.text: Cache capacity in megabytes
SATA interface signaling rate in gigabits per second
RPM
Average seek time in milliseconds

explanation: RPM states spindle revolutions per minute. Seek time measures head positioning, cache capacity describes a buffer, and SATA signaling rate describes the interface. These related storage specifications are not the platter rotational speed.

title: Add a capture card
prompt: A technician must install a PCIe x4 capture card. The motherboard documentation confirms an available physical x16 slot supports the card, adequate lanes and clearance. What is the appropriate action?

options.text: Install the x4 card in that compatible x16 slot following the service procedure
Attach the card to a SATA data cable instead of a PCIe slot
Assume the card will gain sixteen lanes because the slot is longer
Install the card in a physically smaller x1 slot without checking support

explanation: The documented compatible x16 slot can accept this x4 PCIe card. A larger slot does not give the card additional lanes beyond its capabilities. A smaller slot must not be assumed compatible, and SATA is not the expansion-card interface.

title: Recognize an optical patch connector
prompt: A switch transceiver specifies duplex LC fiber connections. Which cable termination should the technician select?

options.text: A fiber patch cord with matching LC connectors and the required fiber type
A fiber patch cord with SC ends that do not match the transceiver
An RJ45 copper patch cable
A BNC coaxial cable

explanation: Match both the LC connector and required fiber type to the transceiver. An SC end will not directly fit an LC socket, while RJ45 copper and BNC coax use different physical media and connectors.

title: Populate a two-channel memory board
prompt: A motherboard manual specifies slots A2 and B2 for a matched two-module memory kit. Which TWO actions best support the intended configuration?

options.text: Mix unsupported memory generations with equal capacity
Judge success only from fan operation without checking detected memory
Install the supported matched modules in A2 and B2
Confirm both modules and the expected capacity are recognized after installation
Use A1 and A2 solely because they are adjacent

explanation: Use the board-specific slot map rather than assuming physical adjacency identifies channels. Verify recognized capacity and configuration afterward. Equal capacity does not make incompatible memory generations interchangeable.

title: Configure scan delivery
prompt: A multifunction printer must place scans in a designated network folder. Its network connection works. Which configuration is directly required for this workflow?

options.text: The folder destination and an account with suitable write permission
Only the paper tray duplex default
Only a local USB print queue on an unrelated workstation
Only the fax telephone number

explanation: Configure a supported network-folder destination and credentials with the necessary write access. Paper defaults, fax dialing and an unrelated local print queue do not authorize or direct network scan storage.

title: Service an impact printer
prompt: An impact printer produces uniformly faint characters on the top sheet and its fabric ribbon is visibly worn. The printhead and feed mechanism pass their tests. What maintenance is most appropriate?

options.text: Replace the ribbon with the specified cartridge
Change the network queue address
Increase print-server spool space
Replace the impact printhead despite its passing diagnostic

explanation: The fabric ribbon supplies ink to an impact printer, and the worn ribbon matches the faint output. The passing printhead test argues against replacing that assembly first. Spool space and queue addressing do not restore the missing ribbon ink.

title: Recognize a desktop hypervisor
prompt: A student installs virtualization software as an application on an existing desktop operating system, then creates two guest VMs. Which hypervisor category is this?

options.text: Type 1 on bare metal in this installation
An operating-system container sharing the host kernel
A dual-boot system with only one OS running at a time
Type 2, hosted on a general-purpose operating system

explanation: A type 2 hypervisor runs on an existing general-purpose operating system. Type 1 describes bare-metal virtualization. An OS container shares a kernel, while ordinary dual boot runs one selected operating system at a time rather than the stated concurrent guests.

title: Limit infrastructure to one organization
prompt: A company uses cloud infrastructure reserved exclusively for its organization, with self-service provisioning for internal teams. Which deployment model best describes this?

options.text: Hybrid cloud integrating separate private and public clouds
Community cloud shared by several independent organizations
Public cloud
Private cloud

explanation: A private cloud is reserved for one organization. Public cloud serves a broader customer population, community cloud serves a defined group of organizations, and hybrid cloud integrates distinct cloud environments. The exclusive-use requirement identifies private cloud here.

title: Connect a VM to the physical LAN
prompt: A training VM must receive its own address from the office DHCP server and be reachable directly by other permitted LAN hosts. Which TWO statements fit a bridged virtual network?

options.text: The VM appears as a separate network participant on the physical LAN
The VM is limited to communicating with guests on a private virtual switch
Bridging automatically bypasses physical LAN access policies
The VM must still comply with the LAN address and access policies
The VM shares the host address through NAT for every inbound connection

explanation: Bridging attaches the VM network interface to the external LAN so it can obtain an address there when policy permits. Bridging does not bypass access controls, guarantee authorization or require host NAT. Isolated and NAT networks serve different purposes.

title: Combine a private cloud with public capacity
prompt: A retailer retains a private cloud for internal services and integrates it with public-cloud resources for seasonal demand. Which deployment model is illustrated?

options.text: Community cloud shared exclusively by organizations with common needs
Hybrid cloud
Public cloud only
Private cloud only, with no integration to another cloud

explanation: Integration of private and public cloud resources describes hybrid cloud. Neither public-only nor private-only describes both parts, and a community cloud is organized around shared needs of a group of organizations.

title: Use a virtual workstation remotely
prompt: An employee uses a thin client to access a centrally hosted desktop with company applications. The desktop continues running in the data center when the employee disconnects. Which solution is this?

options.text: Virtual desktop infrastructure
A local dual-boot installation
A locally installed desktop operating system with only cloud file synchronization
A remotely mounted storage share with all desktop processing on the thin client

explanation: VDI presents a centrally hosted desktop to a remote client. Local dual boot and a locally installed desktop execute at the endpoint; merely mounting shared storage does not move desktop processing to the data center.

title: Explain shared cloud infrastructure
prompt: A cloud provider serves several unrelated customers from a pool of physical resources while logically separating their environments. Which concept is illustrated?

options.text: A dedicated physical host reserved for one customer only
A direct-attached storage appliance with no resource pool
An isolated on-premises workstation
Multitenancy

explanation: Multitenancy shares pooled infrastructure among customers with logical separation. A dedicated customer-only host, isolated workstation or unpooled direct-attached appliance does not describe that shared tenant model.

title: Prepare a disposable test environment
prompt: A technician needs to test an unfamiliar operating-system installer without repartitioning the work laptop. Which approach best meets the requirement?

options.text: Use dual boot by repartitioning the host disk
Run the installer against the existing host system partition
Create a restore point and allow the installer to overwrite the host OS
Create a VM with a new virtual disk and the required resources

explanation: A VM with a separate virtual disk supports testing the guest installer without repartitioning or overwriting the host OS. Dual boot changes the host disk layout, and a restore point is not a guarantee against damage from an OS installer overwriting that disk.

title: Support metered cloud purchasing
prompt: A team selects cloud services billed according to measured use. Which TWO practices align with that purchasing model?

options.text: Track consumption against the team budget
Keep abandoned resources indefinitely because they cannot incur charges
Assume shutting down one VM deletes all its billable storage
Assume every metered service has a fixed monthly bill regardless of usage
Remove unneeded billable resources when the work ends

explanation: Measured consumption allows charges to vary with resource usage. Monitoring use and removing unnecessary billable resources help control it. Compute, retained storage and other resources can have separate billing; stopping a VM does not imply all charges cease.

title: Classify two purchased cloud services
prompt: A clinic purchases a ready-to-use browser appointment application. It separately rents cloud virtual machines on which its own staff install and patch the operating systems. Which pairing correctly classifies these two purchases?

options.text: Appointment application: IaaS; rented VMs: SaaS
Appointment application: PaaS; rented VMs: SaaS
Appointment application: SaaS; rented VMs: IaaS
Appointment application: SaaS; rented VMs: PaaS

explanation: The finished browser application is SaaS. Renting virtual machines while managing their guest operating systems is IaaS. PaaS provides a managed application platform and does not describe customer-managed VM operating systems in this ticket.

title: A new build shuts off under the bench test
prompt: A newly assembled PC shuts down shortly after power-on. The cooler fan spins, but the technician finds the protective plastic film still covering the cooler contact surface. What should be done?

options.text: Power down and reinstall the cooler correctly, removing the film and applying the specified thermal interface material
Replace RAM without inspecting the cooler interface
Increase CPU voltage
Disable thermal shutdown

explanation: The film prevents proper heat transfer even when the fan spins. Correct the cooler installation with power isolated and follow thermal-interface instructions. Raising voltage or disabling thermal protection worsens the thermal risk.

title: A drive disappears only after transport
prompt: After a desktop is transported, firmware no longer lists its SATA data drive. There are no unusual mechanical noises. What is the most appropriate initial physical check with the machine powered off and unplugged?

options.text: Replace the drive immediately without checking connections
Repair the operating-system bootloader before checking detection
Initialize and format the drive
Inspect and reseat the drive data and power connections

explanation: Inspect the SATA data and power path after transport with power isolated. A disconnected drive can disappear from firmware. Formatting, bootloader repair and premature replacement do not establish whether the simple connection path is intact.

title: A conference screen says no signal
prompt: A laptop detects an external monitor through HDMI and works with another screen. The conference display is powered on but its menu shows DisplayPort selected. What should the technician do first?

options.text: Reinstall the laptop operating system
Change the laptop IP address
Select the HDMI input connected to the laptop
Replace the laptop HDMI connector immediately

explanation: Select the HDMI input actually connected to the laptop. The display is listening to another source. Successful laptop output to another display supports correcting the known input mismatch before reinstalling software or replacing its connector; IP settings are unrelated.

title: A phone becomes hot in a vehicle
prompt: A phone left on a dashboard displays an over-temperature warning and stops charging. Which response is most appropriate?

options.text: Disconnect charging and move the phone out of direct heat, allowing it to cool as the manufacturer directs
Bypass the temperature warning with repeated restarts
Put the phone in a freezer while it remains connected to power
Cover the phone with insulation and continue charging

explanation: Remove external heat and charging load and allow safe cooling according to the manufacturer. Freezing can cause condensation or damage; insulation and repeated restarts do not address overheating. Investigate further if the warning persists in normal conditions.

title: Find the shared network outage
prompt: Six desktops on one access switch lose connectivity at the same time. Their link LEDs are off, and the switch power indicator is dark. Other office switches work. Which TWO checks most directly address the common failure?

options.text: Verify power at the affected switch outlet or power source
Check the affected switch power supply and power connection
Replace all six desktop patch cables before inspecting switch power
Change DNS resolvers on the six desktops
Renew leases on the six desktops before restoring the switch

explanation: The simultaneous loss of link and dark switch indicator point to a shared power problem. Verify the power source, connection and supply safely. DHCP, DNS and six independent patch-cable replacements do not restore power to the switch.

title: A printer stops at the same paper position
prompt: A laser printer repeatedly jams at the input area. The loaded paper is visibly curled from moisture, while a fresh sealed ream of the supported size feeds correctly. What is the most appropriate correction?

options.text: Restart the print spooler after every jam
Install a different printer driver without changing the paper
Replace the fuser immediately
Replace the affected paper and store stock in the recommended dry conditions

explanation: The successful test with fresh supported paper isolates the fault to the damp, curled stock. Replace and store the paper correctly. Replacing the fuser, restarting the spooler or changing the driver does not correct the demonstrated feed-media condition.

title: A desktop will not power on after service
prompt: After a case transplant, a desktop shows a motherboard standby LED but the case power button does nothing. The front-panel power-switch plug is connected to the reset pins. What is the corrective action?

options.text: Reconnect the case power-switch lead to the documented power-switch header pins with power disconnected
Reinstall the operating system
Replace the PSU immediately without correcting the known header error
Replace the boot drive

explanation: Correct the misplaced case power-switch lead using the board documentation with power disconnected. The known header error explains the missing power-on signal. Replacing storage or the OS does not fix that circuit, and replacing the PSU first ignores the identified connection error.

title: A hard drive clicks and drops offline
prompt: A hard drive containing unrecovered client data begins repeated clicking and disconnects during reads. The organization has a professional recovery procedure. What is the best next action?

options.text: Stop unnecessary access and follow the approved data-recovery escalation process
Initialize and format the disk to repair its file system
Run repeated full-surface write tests immediately
Continue restarting the drive until the noise disappears

explanation: Clicking with repeated disconnects suggests a possible mechanical failure. Further operation or destructive writes may reduce recovery prospects. Preserve the drive and follow the approved recovery process; do not format irreplaceable data.

title: An image is stretched on a new monitor
prompt: A new 16:9 monitor shows stretched circles. It is being driven at a 4:3 resolution; its native 16:9 resolution is supported by the computer and cable. What should be changed?

options.text: Change only the HDMI audio output device
Replace the monitor before changing its resolution
Increase brightness without changing resolution
Select the monitor native resolution and suitable scaling

explanation: The 4:3 source is being stretched to a 16:9 display. Select the supported native resolution with suitable scaling. Brightness and HDMI audio settings do not correct geometry, and replacing the monitor before addressing the mismatch is premature.

title: Find a sudden battery drain
prompt: A phone used to last a workday. Since a new navigation app was installed, battery usage reports show that app consuming most of the charge while running in the background. What is the best initial action?

options.text: Increase brightness and leave background navigation unrestricted
Review and restrict the app background activity and location use as appropriate, then retest
Replace the battery immediately without checking app activity
Factory-reset the phone without investigating the usage report

explanation: The battery-usage evidence identifies the navigation app as the new major load. Adjust unnecessary background/location use and retest before replacing hardware or performing a disruptive reset. Increasing brightness while leaving the activity unchanged adds another load.

title: The new access point cannot serve clients
prompt: A new access point has power and advertises its SSID, but connected clients cannot reach the wired LAN. The Ethernet uplink was never patched into the switch. What is the most direct correction?

options.text: Change only the client DNS server
Connect and verify the intended Ethernet uplink according to the network design
Increase the radio transmit power without connecting an uplink
Replace all client Wi-Fi adapters

explanation: Connect and verify the intended uplink. Advertising an SSID and associating clients proves radio operation but not upstream LAN connectivity. More transmit power, different DNS or wholesale adapter replacement does not connect the missing wired path.

title: A color print has the wrong colors
prompt: A printer test pattern shows one ink color missing, and the corresponding cartridge is empty. The other cartridges and paper path are normal. What should the technician do?

options.text: Replace the empty cartridge with a compatible one and run the prescribed verification
Clean the paper pickup rollers
Reinstall the network queue without replacing ink
Adjust the document color profile to compensate for the empty cartridge

explanation: Replace the identified empty cartridge and follow the printer verification procedure. The local test pattern isolates the color supply. Roller cleaning addresses feed problems; queue or profile changes cannot replenish ink.

title: Isolate intermittent memory errors
prompt: A workstation reports memory errors after a two-module upgrade. Both modules are supported. Which TWO actions most directly help isolate a bad module or slot?

options.text: Reformat the system disk before running diagnostics
Run the platform memory diagnostic
Test modules individually in supported slots according to the service procedure
Replace the CPU immediately without module or slot testing
Change memory voltage to unsupported values

explanation: Use memory diagnostics and controlled testing of supported modules and slots to isolate the fault. Follow the service procedure and supported settings. Reformatting storage, random voltage changes and immediate CPU replacement do not provide that isolation.

title: An external drive needs more power
prompt: A bus-powered external HDD repeatedly disconnects through an unpowered hub when several other devices are attached. It works reliably on the computer USB port by itself. What should the technician try?

options.text: Disable storage health monitoring
Use a suitable powered hub or the verified direct port
Repartition the drive
Replace the drive immediately without testing the hub path

explanation: The direct-port comparison makes the shared hub path or power supply the first area to address. Test a suitable powered hub or use the reliable direct port. Repartitioning, immediate drive replacement or disabling health reports does not resolve the demonstrated connection dependence.

title: A projector shuts down during presentations
prompt: A projector shows a temperature warning and shuts down after several minutes. Its air filter is clogged and the intake is blocked by a bag. What should be done?

options.text: Increase lamp output to maximum
Disable the shutdown protection
Wrap the projector tightly to keep dust away
Let it cool, clear ventilation and service the filter as documented

explanation: Blocked airflow and a clogged filter explain the overheating. Cool the device and restore documented ventilation and filter maintenance. Higher lamp output or tighter covering increases the thermal burden; bypassing protection is unsafe.

title: A touch screen responds without contact
prompt: A tablet begins registering phantom touches after a cracked screen repair. The problem occurs before any user app launches and remains after removing its case. Which component or installation should be checked?

options.text: The replacement digitizer and its connections
Recreate the wireless profile
Clear only the browser cache
Replace the tablet battery without testing the input assembly

explanation: The service timing, phantom touches and occurrence before user applications point to the replacement digitizer or its connections. Wi-Fi profiles, browser cache and an untested battery replacement do not target the false-touch input path.

title: Resolve a local address mismatch
prompt: Two directly connected devices must communicate on a documented 192.168.70.0/24 LAN. One is 192.168.70.20/24; the other was manually set to 192.168.71.30/24. There is no router between these subnets. What should change?

options.text: Replace the Ethernet switch solely because the subnets differ
Assign both devices the same IPv4 address
Assign the second device an unused authorized address in 192.168.70.0/24
Change only the second device DNS server

explanation: The second device needs an unused authorized address on the intended /24 LAN. Changing DNS does not establish a missing route, using the same address creates a conflict, and changing the switch does not correct the manual subnet mismatch.

title: The printer is waiting for the wrong paper
prompt: A queue sends A4 jobs to a printer whose selected tray is configured for Letter. The printer pauses and requests A4, while its internal Letter test page prints normally. What should be corrected?

options.text: Restart the spooler while retaining the same conflicting media settings
Change the queue IP address
Replace the toner cartridge
Align the job paper-size selection and tray media configuration with the intended loaded media

explanation: Match the intended job paper size, loaded media and tray configuration. The request for A4 is explained by the mismatch, while the local Letter page confirms the printer can print. Toner, spooler restarts and queue addressing do not resolve conflicting media settings.

title: A new firewall policy breaks name lookups
prompt: Immediately after a firewall change, clients can contact an internal service by IP but cannot resolve its name. A capture shows DNS requests to the approved resolver being dropped by the new policy. Which TWO actions are appropriate?

options.text: Change the service IP without updating its DNS record
Retest resolution of the required name after the change
Disable all firewall filtering permanently
Replace all workstation NICs
Correct the policy to allow authorized DNS traffic to the approved resolver

explanation: Correct the scoped firewall rule and verify name resolution. The capture already shows dropped DNS requests; authorized DNS may use UDP or TCP 53. Replacing NICs, disabling all filtering or randomly changing the service IP ignores the specific evidence.

title: Unexpected restart under graphics load
prompt: A desktop is stable at idle but abruptly restarts after a high-power GPU upgrade when a graphics workload begins. Temperatures remain normal, and the installed PSU is below the GPU vendor recommended system capacity. What should be investigated first?

options.text: The CPU thermal interface despite normal monitored temperatures
The monitor native resolution setting
The SATA boot order
PSU capacity, required GPU power connections and power delivery under load

explanation: Investigate PSU capacity and GPU power connections under load. The new high-power GPU and inadequate supply specification support this before unrelated boot-order or display changes. Normal measured temperatures make thermal-interface work a less supported first action.

title: A mirror remains degraded after replacement
prompt: A supported replacement disk has been installed in a degraded RAID 1 array. The controller shows it as ready, but no rebuild has begun and the mirror still has only one synchronized member. What is the next action?

options.text: Initialize the healthy member as an empty disk
Assume inserting the disk has already copied every block
Initiate or enable the documented rebuild and monitor its progress
Remove the healthy member to force the new disk online

explanation: A replacement is not a synchronized mirror until the controller rebuild completes. Follow the controller procedure and monitor progress while retaining a verified backup. Initializing or removing the healthy member puts the surviving data at risk.

title: Diagnose an Ethernet duplex mismatch
prompt: A legacy 100 Mb/s Ethernet link stays up but performs poorly. The switch is forced to full duplex, the client is forced to half duplex, and interface counters show collision-related errors. Both support compatible auto-negotiation. What is the best corrective action?

options.text: Change the DNS resolver while retaining the forced duplex settings
Restore compatible auto-negotiation on both ends according to the network configuration policy
Increase the IP packet size while retaining the duplex mismatch
Renew the DHCP lease without changing either Ethernet interface

explanation: The two ends disagree about duplex operation. Configure matching supported negotiation settings on both ends, then verify the negotiated link and error counters. DNS, packet size and lease renewal do not resolve the stated Ethernet duplex mismatch.

title: A network printer changed addresses
prompt: A printer works from its local test controls, but a desktop queue remains offline after the printer received a different DHCP address. The queue still targets its former IP. What should be done?

options.text: Change the printer paper-size defaults
Update the queue destination and arrange a stable approved printer address
Replace the imaging drum
Restart the spooler without correcting its destination

explanation: Correct the stale queue destination and use an approved stable addressing arrangement, such as a DHCP reservation. Restarting the spooler without fixing its target leaves the cause in place. Drum replacement and paper settings do not affect the queue destination.
